sections.eli10:
### Question 1

Think of your food like a big LEGO castle. Digestion is taking the castle apart into single LEGO bricks so they are small enough to fit through a tiny door. That taking-apart step, using both your teeth and special juices, is digestion. Later, carrying the loose bricks through the door into your body is a different step called absorption.

### Question 2

The small intestine is like a super-long carpet folded up inside you, and the carpet is covered in tiny fuzzy fingers. All that fuzz gives a huge amount of surface to grab nutrients, kind of like how a towel soaks up more water than a flat plastic sheet. That is why almost all the good stuff from your food gets picked up there.

### Question 3

Imagine a big blob of oil floating in water. It is hard to clean because it clumps together. Dish soap breaks that blob into lots of tiny droplets so it is easier to wash away. Bile works like that soap for the fat in your food, breaking one big fat blob into many little ones so the fat-digesting helpers can reach all of it. Bile is also a little bit like baking soda and helps calm the sour stomach juice, but the pancreas pours in most of that calming liquid. Soap for fat is bile's real specialty.

### Question 4

If you wanted to soak up spilled juice fast, a scrunched-up crinkly towel grabs way more than a flat one because it has more surface touching the juice. Villi and microvilli are all those crinkles and fuzz in your gut, giving a giant amount of surface so nutrients get soaked up quickly.

### Question 5

Mechanical digestion is like smashing a cracker into crumbs with your hands. The crumbs are smaller, but they are still cracker. Chemical digestion is like a magic juice that actually turns the cracker crumbs into something totally new and tiny. Smashing first just makes it easier for the magic juice to reach every bit.

### Question 6

Some tools only switch on in the right conditions, like a glow stick that only lights up after you snap it. The stomach's acid is the 'snap' that turns on the protein-cutting tool called pepsin. The sour acid also acts like a guard, zapping germs that sneak in with your food.

### Question 7

Fat-soluble vitamins hitch a ride inside fat, like passengers riding in a car. Bile is what breaks the fat into little cars that can drive through the gut wall. If bile is blocked, the cars never get built, so the vitamin passengers get stranded and leave your body instead of being absorbed.

### Question 8

The small intestine is your body's grabbing zone for nutrients. If you cut out a big chunk of the grabbing zone, there is less carpet and fuzz to catch the good stuff, so a lot of it slips past unabsorbed. Less grabbing area means less nutrition getting into the body.

### Question 9

Ever notice a plain cracker starts tasting a little sweet if you chew it for a long time? That is because spit has a helper called amylase that snips the tasteless starch into small sweet sugars. That snipping of bonds is real chemical digestion, and it starts right in your mouth.

### Question 10

The large intestine is like a sponge that soaks water back out of leftover food so what leaves your body is firm. If the leftovers race through too fast, the sponge does not get enough time to soak up the water, so what comes out is runny and wet. That is what diarrhea is.

### Question 11

After nutrients get grabbed, they take one of two roads home. Sugars and amino acids take the fast blood highway straight to the liver, the body's inspection station. Big fats are too greasy for that road, so they ride a separate milky path called the lymph first, then hop onto the blood later. Two nutrients, two different roads.

### Question 12

The pancreas does two big jobs at once: it sends in a whole toolkit of food-cutting helpers, and it pours in a baking-soda-like liquid to calm down the stomach acid. If it stops, the food does not get cut up properly and the gut stays too sour, which even breaks the few helpers that are left. So digestion of sugars, proteins, and fats all suffer.
